# Edge-function secrets and build environment

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/check-edge-secrets.mjs. Do not edit by hand: change the EDGE/WEB tables in that script and run `node scripts/check-edge-secrets.mjs --write`. -->

Every environment name the edge functions and the web build read, generated from the code (US-392). 69 names are read by edge functions, plus 3 deprecated aliases still honoured for one release. No values live here; a value belongs in the place the "Set in" column names.

The pre-commit hook and CI fail when a function reads a name that is not listed here, when this file is out of date, or when `env.example` stops matching the `VITE_*` names the app reads.

## Where values are set

- **Supabase secret**: `supabase secrets set NAME=...` or the Supabase dashboard (Edge Functions, Secrets). On the self-hosted stack, the functions service environment in Coolify. Functions read them at cold start, so redeploy or restart the functions after a change.
- **Injected by Supabase**: the hosted runtime provides it. The self-hosted functions container needs it in its environment.
- **Cloudflare Pages env**: Pages project, Settings, Environment variables, for Production and Preview. `VITE_*` names are baked into the bundle at build time, so a change needs a new deploy.

## Renames in progress

Five names were in use for two URLs. Functions now read the canonical name through `supabase/functions/_shared/app-urls.ts` and fall back to the old names, logging `[env] NAME is deprecated; set CANONICAL` when one is used, so a project that only has the old secret keeps working.

| Canonical | Deprecated aliases, in fallback order | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `SITE_URL` | `FRONTEND_URL`, `APP_URL` | Public origin of the web app, e.g. https://brikly.net. APP_URL held the full subscription-page URL, so only its origin is used. |
| `PUBLIC_FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` | `FUNCTIONS_URL` | Public base URL that serves function `x` at `${base}/x`, e.g. https://functions.brikly.net. |

To finish a rename: set the canonical secret to the value the alias holds (the first alias that is set wins today), redeploy, confirm the deprecation line is gone from the function logs, then delete the alias secret. A release after that, remove the alias from `ENV_ALIASES` and this script regenerates the table.

| `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` | optional | Supabase secret | outlook-calendar-auth, outlook-calendar-callback, sync-calendar | Same as MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID. |

| `MOZ_SECRET_KEY` | optional | Supabase secret | sync-backlinks | Same as MOZ_ACCESS_ID. |
| `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` | optional | Supabase secret | oauth-proxy | oauth-proxy signs OAuth state with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY instead. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | optional | Supabase secret | 18 functions, listed below | AI features configured for OpenAI fail; the rest are unaffected. |
| `PAGESPEED_INSIGHTS_API_KEY` | optional | Supabase secret | check-core-web-vitals, seo-audit | SEO audits and Core Web Vitals checks skip PageSpeed data. |
| `PUBLIC_FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` | optional | Supabase secret | oauth-proxy, send-intervention-email | oauth-proxy defaults to https://functions.brikly.net, which must match the redirect URI registered with Google and Apple. commercial-email derives SUPABASE_URL/functions/v1; with neither, marketing mail goes out without a List-Unsubscribe link. |
| `QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID` | required | Supabase secret | quickbooks-callback, quickbooks-connect, quickbooks-disconnect, quickbooks-sync | QuickBooks connect, sync and disconnect fail. |
| `QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_SECRET` | required | Supabase secret | quickbooks-callback, quickbooks-connect, quickbooks-disconnect, quickbooks-sync | Same as QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID. |
| `QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT` | required | Supabase secret | quickbooks-callback, quickbooks-sync | Anything but "production" talks to the Intuit SANDBOX API, so production customers sync nothing real. |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | required | Supabase secret | 9 functions, listed below | Mail sent through Resend fails: notifications, booking confirmations, payment and renewal reminders, safety and support notices, trial and funnel email. |
| `SEARCH_CONSOLE_SITE_URL` | optional | Supabase secret | bing-search-api, bing-webmaster-api, google-search-console-api, seo-analytics | Defaults to the brikly.net property. This is a Search Console property id, not the app URL. |
| `SENDGRID_API_KEY` | optional | Supabase secret | send-scheduled-emails, send-seo-notification | send-scheduled-emails and SEO notification email fail or are skipped. |
| `SERP_API_KEY` | optional | Supabase secret | check-keyword-positions, track-serp-features | check-keyword-positions saves Math.random() positions, volumes and difficulty as if they were real rankings. |
| `SITE_URL` | optional | Supabase secret | 12 functions, listed below | Defaults to https://brikly.net. Links in email (invoices, estimates, invites, payment and renewal reminders, blog posts) and SSO/OAuth redirects point there, so a staging project without it sends users to production. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` | optional | Supabase secret | send-seo-notification | SEO Slack alerts are skipped unless the request carries its own webhook. |
| `STRIPE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | required | Supabase secret | store-stripe-keys | store-stripe-keys throws; a company cannot save its own Stripe keys. |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | required | Supabase secret | 20 functions, listed below | Checkout, subscription changes, the billing portal and payment functions return errors. |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | required | Supabase secret | stripe-webhook | stripe-webhook cannot verify signatures and rejects every event, so subscription state stops following Stripe. |
| `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | platform | Injected by Supabase | 174 functions, listed below | User-JWT clients cannot be built, so auth.getUser fails and authenticated functions return errors. |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | platform | Injected by Supabase | 123 functions, listed below | Service-role clients cannot be built; writes that must bypass RLS fail. oauth-proxy also signs OAuth state with it when OAUTH_STATE_SECRET is unset. |
| `SUPABASE_URL` | platform | Injected by Supabase | 197 functions, listed below | Nothing can reach the database or auth; every function fails. |
| `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` | optional | Supabase secret | capture-lead, handle-demo-request, handle-sales-contact | Lead forms are not bot-checked. Set it only after VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY is live, or every submission is refused. |
| `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` | optional | Supabase secret | twilio-calling, workflow-execution | twilio-calling and workflow SMS steps fail. |
| `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | optional | Supabase secret | twilio-calling, workflow-execution | Same as TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID. |
| `TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER` | optional | Supabase secret | twilio-calling, workflow-execution | Same as TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID. |
| `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` | optional | Supabase secret | send-push-notification | Web push is disabled (logged, not an error). |

Two pairs look like duplicates and are not: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` (sign-in, Search Console) and `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` (Calendar, Analytics) are separate OAuth clients with separate redirect URIs, and `BING_SEARCH_API_KEY` / `MICROSOFT_BING_API_KEY` are keys for two different Bing APIs.

`_shared/ai-service.ts` and `_shared/ai-service-env.ts` compute the key name from the provider (claude, openai, gemini); those reads are counted under the three `*_API_KEY` rows.

## Web build (Cloudflare Pages)

Build command `npm ci && npm run build`, Node from `.nvmrc`. `VITE_*` names are what `src/` reads (`import.meta.env`); the rest are read by `vite.config.ts` at build time. `env.example` lists every `VITE_*` name below.

| Name | Need | Set in | Read in | Without it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` | optional | Cloudflare Pages env (Production and Preview), build time; GitHub secret for ci.yml | vite.config.ts | No source-map upload; production stack traces stay minified. |
| `SENTRY_ORG` | optional | Same as SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN | vite.config.ts | Upload cannot find the organization. |
| `SENTRY_PROJECT` | optional | Same as SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN | vite.config.ts | Upload cannot find the project. |
| `VITE_APP_VERSION` | optional | Cloudflare Pages env (Production and Preview), build time | src/ (import.meta.env), vite.config.ts | Sentry events carry no release, so uploaded source maps never match them. |
| `VITE_EDGE_FUNCTIONS_URL` | optional | wrangler.toml [vars] | src/ (import.meta.env) | Falls back to VITE_SUPABASE_URL/functions/v1. |
| `VITE_POSTHOG_API_KEY` | optional | Cloudflare Pages env (Production and Preview) | src/ (import.meta.env) | Product analytics are off. |
| `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST` | optional | Cloudflare Pages env (Production and Preview) | src/ (import.meta.env) | Defaults to https://app.posthog.com. |
| `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` | optional | Cloudflare Pages env (Production and Preview) | src/ (import.meta.env) | Browser errors are not reported. Set it in production. |
| `VITE_SOURCEMAP` | optional | Build env | vite.config.ts | "true" emits hidden source maps without a Sentry upload. |
| `VITE_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID` | optional | Cloudflare Pages env (Production and Preview) | src/ (import.meta.env) | Diagnostics only. |
| `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | required | Cloudflare Pages env (Production and Preview) | src/ (import.meta.env) | The production build fails (vite.config.ts guard). |
| `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` | required | wrangler.toml [vars] | src/ (import.meta.env) | Falls back to https://api.brikly.net. |
| `VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` | optional | Cloudflare Pages env (Production and Preview) | src/ (import.meta.env) | The Turnstile widget is hidden on lead forms. |

### Sentry release and source maps

The Sentry plugin in `vite.config.ts` uploads hidden source maps only when `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is present at build time, tags them with `VITE_APP_VERSION`, and deletes the `.map` files from `dist/` afterwards. Today only `ci.yml` sets these, and CI does not deploy: the bundle Cloudflare Pages serves is built by Pages itself, so unless the four names are in the Pages env its stack traces are minified.

To enable it on Pages:

1. Add `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` (encrypted), `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT` to the Pages env for Production.
2. `VITE_APP_VERSION` has to change per deploy, and the dashboard cannot reference another variable. Set the build command to `npm ci && VITE_APP_VERSION=$CF_PAGES_COMMIT_SHA npm run build` so the release is the deployed commit.
3. Confirm one deploy: the Pages build log shows the Sentry plugin uploading source maps for that release, and Sentry, Settings, Source Maps lists a release named after the commit SHA. Until someone has done this, treat source-map upload as unconfirmed.
